wedge: The Sikh community's own institution now teaches the skills that pay — inside a platform its youth already trust, in the community's voice, and pointed at building for the Panth.
notes: AISF phases imported (149 lessons, source rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch). Lesson bodies in imported/<track>/; our seva intros + lab checks in ours/<track>/ (merged at build). 'Build for the Panth' capstone + the Claude Code guide + both Sikh Code dojos published (dojo engines in lib/institute/dojo/, content in dojo/*.json, guide in guide/*.json, briefs in capstone/*.json). MLI content complete. Split into two sub-schools (2026-09): the AI School (every track above) and the Cybersecurity School (cyber-* path tracks, modules in cyber/<track>.json).

schools.title: AI School
schools.label: school of artificial intelligence
schools.blurb: The twenty-phase AI-engineering spine, the Sikh Code dojos, the Claude Code guide, and the Build for the Panth capstone — from your first line of Python to a shipped agent.

schools.title: Cybersecurity School
schools.label: school of cybersecurity
schools.blurb: Five paths — foundations, defence, offence, the range, and a track for the teachers running a Khalsa school or a gurdwara youth programme. Our syllabus and framing; the labs themselves are free ranges we send you to, never rehosted.

tracks.title: Setup & Tooling
tracks.summary: Get your environment ready for everything that follows. Reframed browser-first — the code lab runs Python and JavaScript, so local install is optional, not the gate.

tracks.title: ML Fundamentals
tracks.summary: Classical machine learning is still the backbone of most production AI.

tracks.title: Deep Learning Core
tracks.summary: Neural networks from first principles. No frameworks until you build one yourself.

tracks.title: Transformers, Deep Dive
tracks.summary: The architecture that changed everything. Understand every layer.

tracks.title: LLM Engineering
tracks.summary: Put LLMs to work in production applications — prompting, RAG, evals, serving, observability.

tracks.title: Tools & Protocols
tracks.summary: The interfaces between AI and the real world — function calls, tool schemas, Model Context Protocol, Agent Skills, security, governance.

tracks.title: Agent Engineering
tracks.summary: The core of modern AI engineering. Build agents from first principles — the loop, memory, planning, multi-step work.

tracks.title: Math Foundations
tracks.summary: The linear algebra, calculus, probability and optimisation that every model rests on — derived in code, not lecture notes.

tracks.title: Computer Vision
tracks.summary: From pixels to understanding: convolutions, detection and segmentation, vision transformers, video and 3D.

tracks.title: NLP, Foundations to Advanced
tracks.summary: Every layer of language modelling — tokenisation, embeddings, attention, decoding, retrieval, evaluation.

tracks.title: Speech & Audio
tracks.summary: The other half of human communication: recognition, synthesis, and audio models. A reading track — no phase exam yet.

tracks.title: Generative AI
tracks.summary: Diffusion and the generative stack across image, video, audio and 3D. A reading track — no phase exam yet.

tracks.title: Reinforcement Learning
tracks.summary: Agents that learn by acting — value methods, policy gradients, and the RLHF loop behind aligned models. A reading track — no phase exam yet.

tracks.title: LLMs from Scratch
tracks.summary: Build, pre-train and fine-tune a language model end to end — data, tokeniser, training loop, scaling, evaluation.

tracks.title: Multimodal AI
tracks.summary: Models that see, hear, read and reason across modalities — encoders, fusion, and multimodal training. A reading track — no phase exam yet.

tracks.title: Autonomous Systems
tracks.summary: Agents that run unattended and safely — long-horizon planning, recovery, guardrails, human oversight. A reading track — no phase exam yet.

tracks.title: Multi-Agent & Swarms
tracks.summary: Coordination between agents — roles, messaging protocols, negotiation, and emergent collective behaviour.

tracks.title: Infrastructure & Production
tracks.summary: Ship AI to the real world — serving, scaling, caching, cost, monitoring, and incident response.

tracks.title: Ethics, Safety & Alignment
tracks.summary: Build AI that helps people — bias, evaluation for harm, alignment techniques, governance. Not optional.

tracks.title: Capstone Projects
tracks.summary: Eighty-five portfolio-grade project briefs — each a real system to build end to end, measured against a public benchmark.

tracks.title: Sikh Code — Learn Coding
tracks.summary: A from-scratch crash course in programming — variables to classes, taught through an IDE that types itself out and explains every line, live.

tracks.title: Sikh Code — Learn Agentic Coding
tracks.summary: The real Claude Code command set — type / to explore. Every command is a topic, with the why behind it, synced to the docs.

tracks.title: Claude Code Guide
tracks.summary: A plain-English map of Claude Desktop and Claude Code for people with zero coding experience — each feature named, then what it lets you do.

tracks.title: Build for the Panth
tracks.summary: Pick one project and ship it: a Gurbani search tool, a gurdwara event board, an archive-OCR helper, a langar/seva coordinator, or a Punjabi-learning bot. Finishing it plus the phase exams earns the Institute certificate.

tracks.title: Security Foundations
tracks.summary: Before red or blue: what a network actually does, how Linux answers to a shell, what the CIA triad buys you, and how to research a target you have never seen. The pre-security path, done properly.

tracks.title: Blue Team — Defence & Response
tracks.summary: The side of security most people are actually paid for: log triage in a SIEM, incident response, disk and memory forensics, threat intelligence, and malware analysis — practised on real, free blue-team ranges.

tracks.title: Red Team — Offensive Security
tracks.summary: Learn to break in so you can tell someone how to stop it: reconnaissance, scanning, the OWASP Top 10, privilege escalation, and an honest introduction to reverse engineering and binary exploitation.

tracks.title: The Range — Applied Practice
tracks.summary: No new theory. Capture-the-flag boxes, container and Kubernetes escapes, recent CVEs including Log4Shell and Spring4Shell, and a short shelf of genuinely hard machines for when the easy ones stop teaching you anything.

tracks.title: Cyber for Schools & Families
tracks.summary: For the ਸੰਗਤ that teaches: Khalsa school staff, gurdwara youth programmes, and parents. Classroom-ready K-12 cyber curriculum, a free browser cyber range for students, career profiles, and the ransomware guidance a school actually needs.

explore.title: freeCodeCamp
explore.blurb: ~11,000 free interactive challenges across ~15 certifications. Their editor, their tests, their certificate — go straight there.

explore.title: Class Central
explore.blurb: A search engine for ~250,000 online courses from 1,000+ universities and providers. Filter for free — and for a free certificate — by subject, level, and provider, then go take the course at the source.

explore.title: Libre.academy
explore.blurb: A local-first desktop app: 90+ interactive coding courses, no account, native compilers offline — and it turns any technical PDF or EPUB into a course with generated exercises. Its book-derived packs sit under non-commercial and no-derivatives licences, so this stand links out rather than rehosting.

explore.title: SANS Institute
explore.blurb: The security profession's reference shelf: free posters, cheat sheets, security policy templates, and whitepapers, by discipline. Free to download and copyright SANS — licensed for non-commercial use, so this stand links out and rehosts nothing.

explore.title: NICCS · CISA
explore.blurb: The US government's cyber-education portal, and the K-12 classroom resources it funds through CYBER.ORG: curriculum by grade band, a browser-based cyber range free to educators, career profiles, and ransomware guidance written for schools.

resources.title: Loop Library
resources.author: Forward Future
resources.blurb: A free, community-built library of reusable AI-agent “loops” — structured prompts with their own checks and stopping conditions. Worth a visit once you are past the agent-engineering phases and building real workflows.

resources.title: The Coding Interview
resources.author: Matthias Endler (mre)
resources.blurb: A free, MIT-licensed GitHub repo of programming exercises, katas, and interview puzzles across 20+ languages, drawing on Project Euler and Google Code Jam. Good bench practice once the fundamentals phases are done.

resources.title: Awesome Learn to Code
resources.author: md8-habibullah
resources.blurb: A free, hand-picked directory of 150+ beginner-friendly open-source repos — roadmaps, free books, interactive platforms, and project ideas — sorted into 16 categories.

resources.title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
resources.author: Harold Abelson & Gerald Jay Sussman, with Julie Sussman
resources.blurb: The classic MIT computer-science text — how to think about programs, not just syntax. Free to read online (JavaScript edition); the original Scheme edition (MIT Press, 1996) is also freely mirrored.

resources.title: Deep Learning
resources.author: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio & Aaron Courville
resources.blurb: The standard graduate-level reference behind the Institute's ML and deep-learning phases. Free to read online; MIT Press also sells the print edition.

resources.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
resources.author: Martin Kleppmann
resources.blurb: How real systems store, replicate, and process data at scale — the book most working backend and infra engineers keep on the shelf.

resources.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
resources.author: David Thomas & Andrew Hunt
resources.blurb: Craft and judgment for working programmers — the habits the lesson pages don't have room to teach.

resources.title: Cracking the Coding Interview
resources.author: Gayle Laakmann McDowell
resources.blurb: 189 programming interview questions worked end to end — the standard companion once you're bench-practicing with The Coding Interview above.

resources.title: Deep Learning Specialization
resources.author: DeepLearning.AI (Andrew Ng), via Coursera
resources.blurb: Five courses covering neural networks, CNNs, sequence models, and how to structure an ML project — the deep-learning phases' spiritual companion.

resources.title: CS50: Introduction to Computer Science
resources.author: Harvard University (David J. Malan), via edX
resources.blurb: Harvard's legendary intro to computer science and programming — algorithms, data structures, and a real problem set every week.

resources.title: Grokking the Coding Interview: Patterns for Coding Questions
resources.author: Educative.io
resources.blurb: 28 reusable interview patterns instead of memorizing individual problems — a paid, text-based companion to the free interview-prep links above.

resources.title: Udacity Nanodegree programs
resources.author: Udacity
resources.blurb: Project-graded, mentor-supported programs in AI, ML engineering, and data — a paid, structured on-ramp for when self-study needs a deadline and a reviewer.

resources.title: Awesome Cyber Security University
resources.author: Oaker Min (brootware) and contributors
resources.blurb: The CC0 roadmap the Cybersecurity School's four practitioner paths are sequenced from — free, learn-by-doing security training in order, from pre-security to hard boxes. Go to the source when you want the full list rather than our narrowed syllabus.

resources.title: The ultimate list of SANS cheat sheets
resources.author: SANS Institute
resources.blurb: Every SANS cheat sheet in one index — forensics, incident response, pen testing, cloud. Free to download; copyright SANS, licensed for non-commercial use. Bookmark it on your first day in the Cybersecurity School.
